title.narrative: Second Greater Mekong Subregion Tourism Infrastructure for Inclusive Growth Project

description.narrative: The project will help transform secondary GMS central and southern corridor towns into economically inclusive, competitive tourism destinations by improving transport infrastructure, urban environmental services, and capacity to sustainably manage tourism growth. It will boost trade in services and deepen regional cooperation and integration in the GMS and Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). About 97,000 residents are expected to directly benefit from climate-resilient infrastructure development and increased access to economic opportunities. Project investments are prioritized in the ASEAN Tourism Strategic Plan 2015-2025, GMS Tourism Sector Strategy 2016-2025, and national tourism strategies.

Output: Output 1. Urban-rural access infrastructure and urban environmental services improved. Indicator: 73 kilometers of access roads to tourist sites improved (2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 21 Progress/Status: CAM (10.4km): As of March 2024, progress for this indicator is 100%. The DMS, RCS and draft DRP were prepared by GDR/PMCES from August to December 2021. Project was signed on 27 Dec 2021. GDR completed the payment of compensation to 77 AHs, on 6 July 2022. NOL for partial handover of about 8 km of road without social impacts was issue 19 Jan 2022. NOL for the final handover of the entire road works area was issued on 11 July 2022. Progress for this indicator is estimated at 100.00% as the roadway has been fully demarcated and the physical works for the toad construction is estimated at 92.00%

- Contract of TIIGP2-LAO-W02: Nam Ngum Reservoir Access Improvements was awarded on 26 Apr 2021, which includes 7.16 km of concrete road. Progress was 100%. Handover was conducted on 3 Dec 2024.
- Contract of TIIGP2-LAO-W03: Kaeng Yui Waterfall Access Improvements and Western Loop Rural Access Road and Bridge Improvements was signed on 23 Jul 2021, which includes 6.6 km of concrete road and 26 km of DBST road totaling 32.6 km of access road improvement. Progress was 100%. Handover was conducted on 1 Aug 2025.
- Contract of TIIGP2-LAO-W04: Vang Vieng Landfill Improvements was awarded on 19 Feb 2021, which includes 1.55 km of concreate road (0.79 km access road and 0.76km internal roads). Progress was 100%. Handover was conducted on 19 Jul 2024.
- The remaining roads are included package TIIGP2-LAO-W03a: Vang Vieng Urban Renewal, which includes 3.15 km asphalt overlay road improvement. The DED was prepared, and endorsed by ADB. The procurement commenced in Q2 of 2024, the contract was signed on 17 October 2024. Progress was 43.55%. The progress reduced due contract variation to increase the scope of works.
A total 65.6 km road will be improved under these 5 Works packages. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: Output 1. Urban-rural access infrastructure and urban environmental services improved. Indicator: Three ferry ports constructed (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: CAM (2): As of June 2024, progress for this indicator is 100%. ADB authorized the start of Construction works on 14 November 2021.
A pier redesign was requested by local community and supported by Kep Province in order to increase the mooring capacity. With PMU approval, the Contractor has subcontracted parts of the pier construction to expedite completion by 31 January 2024. The Contractor has completed the detailed investigation survey and the construction of the camp was completed on March 2022. A pier redesign was requested by local community and supported by Kep Province in order to increase the mooring capacity. This additional works and the greater cost for renting the only large barge available for hire was the subject of a CVO-1. The unavailability of suitable barge affected the transportation of equipment and material to the island caused a delay of works under this subproject.

- Contract for Package TIIGP2-LAO-W02: Nam Ngum Reservoir Access Improvements was awarded on 26 April 2021, which includes passenger/ferry port improvement. Overall progress of the subproject was 100%.
A total of 2 passenger/ferry ports have been improved.
